L55: Michigan State University Veterinary Medical Center Medical Oncology Service, Microbiology & Molecular Genetics Laboratory, and Precision Health Program
L56: 
L57: Study Title: Efficacy and safety of a novel anti-cancer therapeutic for the treatment of metastatic mammary carcinoma in cats
L58: Purpose of Study: Mammary tumors are a commonly encountered cancer in cats, particularly in females, with 80-90% of masses diagnosed as malignant (carcinoma). Mammary carcinoma in cats parallels breast cancer in humans with regards to receptor expression profile and propensity of metastasis. The median survival time in cats ranges from 6 months to several years, depending on tumor size and grade. Greater than 60% of cats have more than one tumor at diagnosis, with the majority being high grade.
L59: The objective of this study is to evaluate the safety and efficacy of a novel therapeutic targeting miR-10b, a molecule responsible for viability of metastatic cells in cats with mammary carcinoma. This multipurpose therapy has a previously demonstrated efficacy in halting breast cancer invasion and metastasis in mice. The advantage of our novel therapeutic over existing drugs is that it can also be used to visualize primary and metastatic lesions in vivo by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI).
L60: Studies in cats with mammary carcinoma will help bring this therapeutic into clinic to treat human breast cancer.
L61: Inclusion Criteria (may be evaluated at MSU or at primary care):
L62:   * Histologic or cytologic diagnosis confirmatory of mammary carcinoma with metastasis
L63:   * Diagnosis of metastatic lesions confirmed via cytology/histopathology if accessible, or based on clinical suspicion
L64:   * Non-ulcerated primary/external mammary carcinoma lesions, total volume up to 8 cm^{3}, subject to the overall health evaluation
L65:   * Overall health criteria, adequate liver function, adequate renal function, expected survival >4 weeks
L66:   * Lymph node metastasis, or any other metastatic invasion to be confirmed by cytology and/or CT scan
L67:   * Cases that have not undergone surgery or have undergone unilateral or bilateral mastectomy with metastatic involvement will be included
L68:   * Tumors with or without prior chemotherapy, concurrent NSAIDs are allowed
L69:   * Confirmed microRNA-10b overexpression > log 2 in lesion vs non-tumor parenchyma
L70:   * Informed client consent signed and willingness to consent to drug administration at multiple intervals, blood draws, return visits, monthly CT scans, post-mortem examination
L71: Study Treatment: Cats with metastatic mammary carcinoma will first undergo a baseline CT scan. Cats will also undergo diagnostic imaging (MRI) before and 24 hours after the injection of the therapeutic to ensure its accumulation in the tumor lesion(s). For all imaging (MRI or CT scan) cats will be maintained under anesthesia using routine anesthesia methods and will be monitored closely by veterinary specialists.
L72: After the first injection, treatment will be repeated in two weeks followed by monthly CT scans and treatments. The follow up period may be extended for up to 12 months after initial treatments based on response.
L73: Compensation: This is a funded study: cats will receive the investigational therapeutic and associated imaging free of cost. Pet owners are financially responsible for all treatments and diagnostics that are unrelated to the study.
L74: 
L75: Contact Information: Please feel free to contact our Medical Oncology Team at (517) 353-5420 or cvm.oncoinfo@msu.edu to refer a patient or for any additional information. Referring veterinarian and client calls are welcome.

L53: Clinical Study: Time to Maximal Response to Neoadjuvant Corticosteroids in Dogs with Mast Cell Tumors
L54: 
L55: Purpose of Study:
L56: Mast cell tumors (MCT) are the most common skin tumor in dogs. MCTs can be treated in a variety of ways, with surgery being a common component of care. When MCTs are located in a challenging surgical location, we will try pre-treating with drugs to shrink the tumor and give the surgeon more flexibility. Historically, these pre-surgical treatments include chemotherapy and/or corticosteroids. Anecdotally, if the MCT shrinks, the effect only lasts for a limited period.
L57: To date, there are no studies identifying the ideal time between starting steroids and performing surgery. In this study, we plan to identify canine patients with cutaneous MCTs, administer corticosteroids, and before proceeding to surgery, clients (pet owners) will obtain daily measurements.
L58: The aim of this study is to identify guidelines for pre-operative steroid treatment with secondary goals of decreasing surgical risks and improving post-operative outcomes in dogs affected by this disease. Identifying an ideal pre-surgical treatment window can improve veterinarian confidence in surgical scheduling, help facilitate successful surgery, and limit the influence of steroids on wound healing.
L59: 
L60: Eligibility Criteria:
L61:   * Inclusion criteria:
L62:     * Confirmed mast cell tumor diagnosis via cytology or histopathology (may be completed through primary veterinarian or at MSU)
L63:     * Cutaneous mast cell tumor located on the trunk (above the elbow or knee)
L64:     * Mast cell tumor measures between 2-6cm in one dimension
L65:     * Bloodwork confirming adequate organ function and ability to undergo general anesthesia (may be completed through primary veterinarian or at MSU)
L66:   * Exclusion criteria:
L67:     * Prior anti-cancer treatment, including steroids, within 7 days
L68:     * Patients on NSAIDs need 5 or more days of washout before enrolling
L69:     * Evidence of MCT metastasis
L70:     * Expected survival < 4 weeks with treatment
L71:     * Diabetes mellitus or other systemic condition that interferes with safe steroid administration
L72: Eligibility Diagnostics:
L73: 
L74: Prior to study entry, pet owners will be responsible for an initial consultation at MSU and to complete the following diagnostics for their dog:
L75: 
L76:   * Cytology or histopathology of tumor in question to confirm diagnosis of MCT (if not already completed)
L77:   * Bloodwork ensuring adequate organ function to undergo general anesthesia (if not already completed)
L78: Staging diagnostics including abdominal ultrasound with cytologic evaluation of regional lymph nodes, spleen, and/or liver will be contingent on a overseeing clinician’s recommendation as well as client election. This is not a requirement for inclusion.
L79: 
L80: Treatment:
L81: Initial caliper measurements of the tumor will be obtained by 2 trained staff members on the day of enrollment. Clients will be trained by MSU staff in caliper usage and each dog will be prescribed prednisone, diphenhydramine, and either famotidine or omeprazole for 14 days.
L82: Each morning, the clients will obtain caliper measurements of the MCT in the 3 planes as instructed per specific training images. Photographs that include the caliper will be emailed to the primary investigators daily. In-person evaluations will be completed at MSU on days 7 and 14 to confirm measurement accuracy and allow for surgical planning.
L83: Surgical resection will be planned for Day 14 (+/- 1 day) with the MSU Soft Tissue Surgery service, and tissue will be submitted for biopsy analysis. Patients who experience significant or rapid tumor shrinkage may undergo surgery sooner.
L84: 
L85: If at any time throughout treatment, the tumor grows by >20%, the patient will be removed from the trial and given appropriate care based on clinician discretion.
L86: 
L87: Compensation:
L88:   * This is a partially funded trial
L89:     * Up to 50% of the surgical fees and the histopathology fees will be covered
L90:     * All trial-specific medications (prednisone, diphenhydramine, famotidine/omeprazole) will be covered once enrolled
L91:     * Calipers will be provided
L92:   * If additional surgery is completed under the same anesthetic event, the client will be financially responsible
L93: 
L94: Contact Information:
L95: Please feel free to contact our Medical Oncology Team at (517) 353-5420 or cvm.oncoinfo@msu.edu to refer a patient or for any additional information. Referring veterinarian and client calls are welcome.

L80: ### 招募犬黑色素瘤及骨肉瘤臨床試驗
L81: #### 招募犬黑色素瘤及骨肉瘤臨床試驗
L82: 
L83: 
L84: 
L85: 台北長青動物醫院總院正在招募罹患黑色素瘤(melanoma)或骨肉瘤(oesteosarcoma)的狗參與臨床試驗！
L86: 
L87: 此次的試驗是將IL15透過噴霧治療形式進行治療。IL15是一種細胞激素，具有促進免疫與抑制腫瘤生長的效果。
L88: 
L89: 有許多人類腫瘤臨床試驗顯示IL-15具有治療腫瘤的潛力，此種藥物最近也被應用在狗的黑色素瘤及骨肉瘤，初步結果指出IL-15對這類患犬同樣具有治療效益。
L90: 
L91: 
L92: 
L93: 試驗目的在於進一步驗證IL15 對於犬黑色素瘤及骨肉瘤長期控制的效果。
L94: 
L95: 關於這個試驗的重點Q&A
L96: 
L97: 1.這項治療的原理是什麼？IL-15是一種細胞激素，能夠刺激自身的免疫細胞（NK細胞、T細胞）對抗腫瘤的生長和轉移。
L98: 2.參加試驗的狗須符合哪些條件a.經細胞學或組織病理學確診罹患黑色素瘤或骨肉瘤。b.患犬品種、年齡、體重、性別不限。c.肺部轉移病灶直徑需大於1.0公分。d.患犬沒有出現危及生命的腫瘤相關症狀。e.目前沒有使用類固醇或其他免疫抑制劑。f. 飼主須能配合每周回診治療追蹤，療程約10~12週。
L99: 
L100: 3.治療過程是如何進行？IL15藥劑以皮下注射方式給藥。若有肺部腫瘤轉移則會將藥劑放置在噴霧機內，患犬在清醒的狀態下佩戴呼吸面罩，含有藥劑的噴霧會隨著呼吸進入狗的肺部。
L101: 
L102: 4.多久需回診一次？每週治療一次，共八次治療。治療結束後兩週需回診追蹤療效。
L103: 
L104: 5.治療過程中需要進行哪些檢驗？治療前需進行血檢、尿檢、X光或電腦斷層確認腫瘤狀態。治療當日需抽血檢查。療程結束後會再次進行血檢、尿檢、X光或電腦斷層評估效果。
L105: 
L106: 6.參加這項試驗的狗可能有什麼副作用？初步的研究顯示腫瘤患犬使用IL15可能發生的副作用為疲倦、嗜睡、肝指數上升、下痢、呼吸加快等，大多數情況下這類副作用並不會危及生命，可自行緩解。
L107: 7.參加這項試驗對我的狗有什麼好處？先前的臨床試驗顯示IL15可以讓部分患犬的腫瘤縮小或消失，參加此次試驗的狗可能達到類似的效果。相較於傳統的血管注射化療，副作用的發生機率與嚴重程度較低。
L108: 
L109: 8.參加試驗需要費用嗎？此次試驗的IL15藥劑不收費，治療過程中所需的檢查及輔助用藥費用需由飼主自行負擔。
L110:
